deities: Lord Shiva (Sukreswar - enshrines one of the largest Shivalingams in India)
Lord Vishnu (subsidiary shrine in the temple premises)

history.period: 1744 by Ahom King Pramatta Singha; financial provisions added by King Rajeswar Singha in 1759
history.summary: The Sukreswar Temple is an important Shiva temple on Sukreswar (Itakhuli) hill on the south bank of the Brahmaputra in the Pan Bazaar locality of Guwahati, enshrining one of the largest Shivalingams in India. The Kalika Purana links the hillock to Saint Sukra, who made his retreat here and meditated on Lord Shiva; the meditating spot, shaped like an elephant's hump, is called Hastagiri. Another tradition says the sage Suka (son of Vyasa) meditated here. It was constructed in 1744 by Ahom King Pramatta Singha (1744-1751), and King Rajeswar Singha (1751-1769), a promoter of the Saiva cult, made financial provisions for the temple in 1759. A long flight of steps leads down from the temple compound to Sukreswar Ghat on the river - famed for sunset views. The complex also has a Vishnu temple, halls for marriages and rituals, and the adjoining Nat Mandir; ruined sculptures and stone fragments on the hill slope suggest religious activity predating the Ahom period. Pind-daan rites for departed ancestors are performed here by devotees.

name: Sukreswar Temple
town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Northeast India, spread along the south bank of the Brahmaputra river in Kamrup Metropolitan district; Dispur, the capital of Assam, is its eastern suburb. Known as the 'City of Temples', it hosts Kamakhya, Umananda, Navagraha, Sukreswar and other historic shrines, plus the IIT Guwahati campus across the river. It is the gateway to the Northeast, well connected by air, rail and road.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport - about 20-25 km.
travel.railway: Guwahati Railway Station - nearest major railhead; temple is in Pan Bazaar in the heart of the city.
travel.road: Pan Bazaar is central Guwahati - easily reached by city bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi from anywhere in the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant weather; the ghat steps are best at sunset).
